mechanism_narrative: A rising GDP indicates strong economic demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns as corporate earnings are likely to improve.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time over the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in unemployment rate suggests labor market weakness, which could lead to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending may decline.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE increases by 0.2pp in one month
failure_condition: If unemployment rate increases but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When both employment and unemployment rate improve, it indicates a strong labor market, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both employment and unemployment improve but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 30% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A rise in federal funds rate indicates tighter monetary policy, which could lead to negative S&P 500 returns as borrowing costs increase.
failure_condition: If federal funds rate increases but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production suggests stronger supply chains and economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If industrial production increases but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts indicates weaker demand in the housing market, which could lead to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If housing starts decline but S&P 500 returns remain positive more than 50% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth is strong but inflation is high, it may indicate demand-pull inflation, which could lead to negative S&P 500 returns as costs rise.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is strong and inflation is high but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in real federal spending indicates increased demand, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns as government spending stimulates economic activity.
failure_condition: If real federal spending increases but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 30% of the time.
